title: Phase 0a: external-gap base rate = 46% (this corpus), winnable 35% — but 12/18 wins are self-benchmark meta
summary: Retrospective classification of 52 completed note-dependent tasks (frequency methodology, method c). External-gap base rate = 24/52 = 46% (the payoff-ceiling indicator); winnable (empirical AND external-gap AND load-bearing) = 18/52 = 35%; empirical 50%, load-bearing 65%. Decision gate NOT tripped (not near-zero) -> winnable regime is real here, don't abandon. CRITICAL CAVEAT: corpus is the orchestrator benchmarking its own memory; 12 of 18 wins are benchmark/memory-meta tasks whose external note is a prior MEASURED verdict — least likely to transfer. Transfer-robust slice = 6/18 (HTTPS issuer-trust, git-substrate-workspace-bound, read-never-write-native, get_full_graph stale+huge, worktree-GC-cruft, concurrency-collision). Customer-workload external-gap more plausibly ~10-15% than 46%. Proxy can't prove load-bearing (no cold arm); ~half the set is self-contained (--L/--- = 25/52). NEXT: small targeted Phase-1 A/B on the 6 transfer-robust wins + 3-4 controls to validate proxy precision/recall, not survey. Report at bench/frequency-phase0a.md.
